title: Guaranteed throughput contracts + predictive autoscaler for tenant fleet separation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a tenant-facing guaranteed throughput contract system plus a predictive autoscaling controller and fleet controls to reduce noisy-neighbor impact while preserving tail latency SLOs. The feature comprises: 1) per-tenant minimum throughput commitments (contracts) expressed in tokens/sec; 2) a predictive autoscaler that uses short-term traffic forecasting to pre-provision lanes and avoid cold-start latency; 3) a fleet-level admission and soft-eviction policy that enforces contracts, reclaims excess burst capacity, and harmonizes placements to reduce cross-tenant interference. This ticket covers design, implementation of scheduler hooks, runtime admission checks, metrics dashboards, e2e testing, and canary rollout for Dedicated clusters.

implementation_notes: We implement a two-path runtime: (A) contract-enforced lanes with guaranteed token allocation and softer bursting subject to local bucket; (B) best-effort lanes that can be preempted. Autoscaler will subscribe to tenant forecasts and create lane reservations ahead of predicted demand using a hysteresis window. Eviction scoring uses a composite metric: contract-violation-risk (weight 0.6), recent-resource-usage(0.2), and interference-index(0.2). Admission controller must tag traces with contract metadata for downstream billing and observability.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary on staging with synthetic tenants (2 days). 2) Canary to 2 Dedicated clusters (72 hours), monitor p95/p99 and cost delta. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of Dedicated clusters; if >5% regression in committed-tenant p99, rollback. 4) Full fleet rollout after 14 days of stable metrics.
rollback_criteria: committed-tenant p99 latency increases >5% sustained for 30m OR unplanned eviction rate >1% of active requests for >15m
testing_strategy: Unit tests for scheduler hooks and admission logic, integration tests with autoscaler simulator, e2e load runs with mixed tenant SLAs, chaos tests (node restart/thermal events) to validate hysteresis and anti-thrash logic.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Pros: predictable SLOs for paying customers, lower tail latency, reduced manual ops. Cons: higher complexity in scheduler and billing integration, potential underutilization if forecasts are poor. Mitigations: conservative hedging in initial contracts, autoscaler fallback to opportunistic reclaiming after 10s of sustained idle, continuous forecast retraining.
human_readable_summary: Ship a tenant-aware throughput guarantee system and a predictive autoscaler to ensure Dedicated customers get stable latency and throughput while reducing noisy neighbor incidents. Includes telemetry, scheduler changes, autoscaler integration, tests, and canary rollout.
